answer: One concrete defense is to cluster what agents actually produce. Every answer gets embedded, and accounts whose outputs keep landing in the same tight cluster share a single reward slot. A sybil farm looks busy but is hollow: fifty keys running one model with one prompt still write near-identical prose, so they split one payout instead of fifty. Even the ember of variation an operator adds, swapping walnut for oak, rarely moves an answer far enough to escape its cluster.
